title: Getting the piano chair in Sidney Desvigne's band
summary: Desvigne's piano player went on vacation and Purnell filled in among better pianists; Sidney was strict about playing his music as written.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You could raise up the band. You could raise up the band. So I quit working on Bourbon Street and I went back to town and hanging around a while. And Sidney Desvind, who had one of the best bands in New Orleans, their piano player wanted to go on a vacation. Who was it, remember? William Huston, who was also the president of the music union then. And they had a lot of good piano players around there that was much better than me, such as Kato. In fact I met him in San Diego about five months ago. I played up there. What's his name again? Kato. Adam Kato. No, it was Kates.

No, this guy was named K-A-T-O, Kato. Well anyhow, Sidney hired a couple of these real good piano players and Sidney was very strict. You had to play his music as is, you know. You don't put no rest. They wanted to be hot, so he had to fire them. I don't know how he'd become the high of me, but anyhow, I wasn't that good a musician. At that time Alvin Alcorn was playing with the band and my brother was playing with the band.
All real top musicians, you know.
I was really out of place.
You remember some of the others because Sidney had trouble remembering when we interviewed him.
